talks.title: The Power of Collaboration to Secure Critical Infrastructure
talks.teaser: Explores the Power of Collaboration to Secure Critical Infrastructure and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview: Sed Bilal presents at S4x25 on securing critical infrastructure through integration and collaboration across security tools and organizational boundaries.

Key Topics: Why critical infrastructure remains a high-value target; vulnerabilities from standalone security tools lacking holistic visibility; real-world collaborative defense examples; and OT/ICS-specific security challenges.

Technical Details: Bilal uses a puzzle metaphor—pieces from different sets cannot form a complete picture, just as disconnected tools leave gaps attackers exploit. He draws on 16 years of OT/ICS experience for integrated platform visibility.

Takeaways: Integration and collaboration are necessities for critical infrastructure defense. Security teams must break down silos between tools and teams to achieve comprehensive threat visibility.

talks.title: Water: The (Potentially) Most Cyber-Resilient CI Sector
talks.teaser: Examines water: The (Potentially) Most Cyber-Resilient CI Sector and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Sector Scale and Security Gaps

The U.S. has 143,000 public water systems with uneven cyber risk. Many small non-community systems lack external connectivity, but community systems face poor security engagement—under 1% adopted free CISA scanning or EPA assessments despite outreach.

Regulatory and Budget Constraints

Without federal cyber regulations and with limited budgets, utilities prioritize compliance-mandated work over voluntary security. High-profile disruptions by groups like Cyber Army of Russia Reborn illustrate the sector's exposure.

Built-in Resilience

Water tanks buffer hours of demand during treatment or pump failures, giving operators time before customer impact. A Massachusetts survey found most utilities can run manual operations, and frequent boil orders and pipe breaks mean operators routinely handle disruptions.

Practical Security Measures

Recommended approaches include independent data loggers parallel to SCADA for tamper detection, reconsidering always-on remote access when alarm-only monitoring suffices, and contingency plans for partial manual operation when PLCs are unavailable.

talks.title: Using Microsoft Detours For Deep System Inspection
talks.teaser: Examines using Microsoft Detours For Deep System Inspection and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
File Operation Vulnerabilities in OT

The speaker opens with SCADA alert managers that write logs using elevated privileges, showing how mispointed config files can corrupt critical binaries and cause endless reboots.

Why Static Analysis Falls Short

Logical file-operation bugs persist across architectures and look benign to automated tools because privileged processes routinely create, move, and delete files.

Microsoft Detours Approach

Dynamic binary instrumentation injects detour functions around syscalls without recompiling targets. Detours is chosen as a lightweight native Windows option versus heavier frameworks like Frida.

Inspection Logic

A DLL hooks high-integrity file operations, filters by integrity level and syscall type, and logs risky create, move, or delete behavior to surface privilege-abuse paths in engineering workstations.

talks.title: ControlLogix PLC Endpoint Hardening
talks.teaser: Reviews controlLogix PLC Endpoint Hardening and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Threat landscape

The speaker argues PLCs are increasingly targeted in critical infrastructure while IT/SCADA layers get better patching and monitoring. DNI and industry data cited show nation-state activity, outdated software, and roughly 12% of assets internet-exposed; oil-and-gas reporting suggests PLCs are hit more than SCADA.

Problem

Rockwell ControlLogix dominates North America, yet few deployments are patched or hardened despite broad critical-infrastructure use.

Defense in depth

Recommendations span physical controls (locking unused USB/SD ports), logical controls (RBAC, SSO via FactoryTalk/AD/Azure AD with MFA), encryption at rest, locking static IPs, disabling unused ports/web pages/SNMP, and keeping controllers in run mode to block remote program-mode changes.

CIP Security focus

Most time covers ODVA-managed CIP Security for authentication, integrity, and confidentiality. FactoryTalk Policy Manager (free) defines zones/conduits on Purdue-model networks and pushes policy to CIP-capable devices. PROFINET, DNP3, and Modbus TCP security are mentioned as less-adopted alternatives.

talks.title: Zones & Conduits In The Cloud
talks.teaser: Provides zones & Conduits In The Cloud and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
## IEC 62443 Meets Cloud OT

A recurring S4x presenter adapts ISA/IEC 62443 zones-and-conduits methodology for cloud-hosted operational technology. As IT and OT support teams converge, organizations question whether cloud-connected industrial systems deserve IT-style management—and how classical OT segmentation maps to virtual infrastructure.

## Zones as Risk Decisions

In 62443, zones group assets sharing security requirements and functional connectivity—not arbitrary network diagrams. Conduits govern controlled communication between zones. The model emphasizes where risk-based security decisions originate rather than drawing boxes and lines.

## Cloud Service Models and Control

IaaS resembles virtual data centers where customers patch OS and middleware. PaaS removes server control but allows application management. SaaS typically exposes only user accounts. Cloud providers own underlying infrastructure; customer responsibility shrinks up the stack, complicating OT asset ownership and patch accountability.

## AI Pressure on OT Cloud Migration

Business units increasingly demand cloud AI for operational analytics, challenging traditional air-gapped OT assumptions. Applying zones-and-conduits in hybrid environments requires mapping SCADA components to cloud tenancy boundaries, identity federation, and conduit policies that preserve safety functions while enabling monitored connectivity.
